the time averaged acoustic force on a cylinder in a viscous fluid depends on the fluid viscosity and the acoustic Reynolds number, which is defined as the ratio between the acoustic particle displacement amplitude and the viscous boundary layer thickness, and the time averaged force on the cylinder in a viscid fluid is smaller than the force in an inviscd fluid.

the numerical results agree with the theoretical solutions and the LB method, and the effects from viscosity can be ignored for the acoustic forces on a single rigid cylinder, but the viscous force is important when considering the secondary force between two rigid cylinders in a standing acoustic field.

the time averaged acoustic force on the cylinder in an ideal fluid is proportional to the square of the amplitude of the sound field, the time averaged acoustic torque on the cylinder is proportional to the product of the sound amplitude and the cylinder radius, and the time averaged acoustic secondary force between two cylinders is proportional to the sound amplitude.

the time averaged acoustic force acting on a single cylinder and two cylinders in an ideal and viscous fluid.
